knowledge.explanation: Leaf yellowing, wilting, spotting and stunting can arise from multiple pests, pathogens or non-biological stresses. The candidate organisms in these training notes are host associations from general knowledge; they do not establish Moroccan occurrence, regional importance or a diagnosis from a photograph.

Wheat epi 1 cm identifies early stem elongation by the position of the developing ear above the tillering node. Sowing date, cultivar, vernalisation and photoperiod affect its calendar date. Sugar-beet bolting involves prolonged cold exposure after developmental competence; it is different from instantaneous frost damage.

A botanical-family change is an incomplete proxy for a pathogen break. Broad-host pathogens, volunteer crops and weeds can maintain inoculum. Disease-specific intervals, crop-specific restrictions and advisory preferences should retain their original scope.

SoilGrids conversion metadata describe mapped units. Soil organic carbon concentration is different from an areal carbon stock; stocks additionally require depth, bulk density and appropriate coarse-fragment handling. RothC separates faster and slower plant-material pools, microbial biomass, humified matter and inert matter. Climate and clay effects are model functions, not crop-damage limits.

Air, canopy, soil and harvested-product temperatures are different measurements. Injury depends on exposure duration, tissue temperature, hardening, cultivar and stage. A chamber treatment is not automatically a daily maximum or minimum threshold.

Grain, fresh pods, roots, fresh forage, dry forage and recoverable sugar are different products. Yield comparisons need matching product, moisture basis, harvest period, region and farming system. A regional mean does not describe a specific field or prove an irrigation response.
